title: Assurance Roadmap — SOC2/ISO Waves & Evidence Queue
creator: Leah Martinez
description: Consolidate the compliance readiness work into time-boxed waves and a prioritized evidence queue so that SOC2 Type II and ISO27001 readiness progress is visible, testable, and reduces last-mile audit churn. This ticket defines waves, owners, acceptance criteria for evidence ingestion, and the automated gating rules for demo-ready artifacts. Outcome: a tracked set of evidence artifacts that map to control IDs, owners assigned, and an automation backlog to reduce manual audit prep by 60% for the May audit milestone.
milestones: Wave 0 (Discovery): control inventory & current-state evidence map completed by 2025-03-15 (Owner: Leah Martinez / Security PM)
Wave 1 (Critical Controls): SSO/SAML, Authn, and Audit Log retention controls implemented and validated by 2025-04-01 (Owner: Eng-Security lead)
Wave 2 (Operational Evidence): CI/CD, deployment change logs, and incident playbooks collected and indexed by 2025-04-20 (Owner: Platform PM)
Wave 3 (Automation & Sampling): evidence ingestion pipeline + sampling tests live by 2025-05-05 (Owner: Data Eng)
Audit Readiness Dry Run: full control walkthrough and evidence bundle for auditors by 2025-05-12 (Owner: Compliance Manager)
Audit Window: provide final evidence and respond to auditor requests by 2025-05-15 (Owner: All)
acceptance_criteria: Every SOC2/ISO control mapped to at least one evidence artifact or a documented mitigation
Evidence artifacts are tagged with control_id, owner, created_at, and storage_location
SSO/SAML flow diagrams, SSO test accounts, and access reviews are recorded in the evidence queue
Audit logs retention policy documented and validated in staging for the last 90 days
Automated ingestion covers >40% of required artifacts at Wave 3; manual playbook covers remainder
Dry run produces no more than 5 high-severity gaps and an action plan to resolve them before audit
risks: Delayed infra changes (log retention hooks) increase manual evidence collection work
Third-party SSO provider changes could require revalidation of flows and replay tests
Underestimated time to tag and reconcile legacy artifacts from pre-2024 deployments
Audit scope creep if auditors request controls outside the current mapping
